rule: Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, ...) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. ... Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. ... **C7 Complete edges.** Caller and callee are never empty.
source: KNOWN_GAP: superclass constructor calls in class headers and infix calls are not emitted; constructor default values get an empty caller
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type or object name) is method; a class-name call `T(..)` that resolves to a constructor, and `: this(..)` / `: super(..)` / a supertype-list call, are constructor. Kotlin has no `new`; a `val x = T(..)` constructor call is treated as decision A's `= new T(...)`. Line 7: the supertype-list call `: Base(name())` is Vec's superclass constructor call (the `: base(...)` form), run by Vec's primary constructor: Vec#<init> → Base#<init>, constructor. The argument `name()` is evaluated in the same place, so its caller is also Vec#<init>. Line 19: `a dot b` is an infix call of the member `infix fun dot`; `a` is a Vec parameter: Vec#dot, method, on the line of `dot`. Line 17: the default value `Clock()` of the primary-constructor parameter `clock` (not a property) is evaluated by the constructor, so its location is Svc#<init>; never an empty caller (C7). Line 10: a function parameter's default `defaultK()` has its function as caller, Vec#scaled, alongside the body's `Vec(x * k)`. Base and Clock have no written constructor; in-scan class, high.
